sentences.text: Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Anshuman G.and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Neha Poonia, Police Station, P.S. Krishna Nagar, Delhi.

6. Brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized according to Sikh Rites and Ceremonies at Gurdwara Harkishan Nagar, Paschim Vihar,
Delhi.
Out of the said wedlock, one male child namely was born on 02.08.2023.
Due to matrimonial disputes, the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 started living separately since 26.07.2023.

It is stated that during the pendency of the case, both the parties have amicably settled all their disputes and the parties are living together as husband and wife along with their minor child happily since 11.03.2024.
7.

On the query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between them and they have been living together since 11.03.2024 along with the minor child.
Respondent no. 2 further stated that she has no objection if FIR may be quashed.
8. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings

,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/06/2024 at 22:53:42 9.

Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 0044/2024, registered at Police Station Krishna Nagar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
10. The petition stands disposed of.
11. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MAY 30, 2024/zp
